name: time-httpdate
algorithm: Make n whole-second instants of 1970 to 2099 (splitmix64, seed 1), then rounds times write each as an IMF-fixdate (RFC 9110 5.6.7, "Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT") and parse the text back; the checksum adds per instant and round the parsed seconds and the text's length, wrapping.

skip.c: C's std has strftime but no parser of the three HTTP date forms (strptime is POSIX, not in the Windows CRT)
skip.rust: Rust's std has no calendar or HTTP date (httpdate is a crate)
skip.zig: Zig's std.http has no date formatter or parser
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the task has no other arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the functions are tested against Go by the lane's Go tests (status/std-time2.md)
notes: Mk: time.FormatHttpDate into an arena per round, freed at its end, then time.ParseHttpDate (IMF-fixdate first, then RFC 850 and asctime). Go: Time.AppendFormat with http.TimeFormat into one reused buffer, then net/http.ParseTime, which tries the three layouts with time.Parse in turn.
Checksums agree between Mk and Go at both sizes on the owner's machine (std-time2 session 2, 2026-11-13).
Not published: no number here is a measurement.
